newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber inches up at close on back of Japan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber inches up at close on back of Japan.

text.p: Rubber futures closed slightly higher on Tuesday in line with higher Japanese prices in moderate trade, dealers said.
"There was a bit of buying for all grades of rubber, mainly encouraged by the increase in Japanese prices this afternoon," a local rubber trader said.
Tokyo's benchmark April contract closed 2.5 yen up at 143.3 while Kobe's April contract gained 2.6 yen to also reach 143.3.
"Some commodity houses who were closing their positions engaged in a bit of selling which matched other people who were doing some shortcovering," another trader said.
Dealers said the market may easily fall back into a stupor in the absence of market-moving news.
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 126.00-128.00 U.S. cents a kg from Monday's settlement of 126.00 cents.
December RSS1 was seen at 180.00-182.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.29) a kg from 179.50 cents.
December TSR20 was seen at 175.00-177.00 Singapore cents (US$1.24-$1.25) a kg from the previous 174.75 cents.
